en.greeting: Hi! You already know can. Today you'll meet its polite, past-time partner: could. Let's go!

steps.title: Could: can in the past
steps.text: Can is for now: **I can swim.** To talk about the past, English changes the word to **could**.
steps.body:
**could** = *dulu bisa*, **couldn't** (could not) = *dulu tidak bisa*. Like can, could is a helper word: the same for everyone, and the verb after it stays in the base form (no -s, no -ed, no to): **When I was five, I could swim.**
The trap: in Indonesian *bisa* never changes (*dulu saya bisa …*). In English the word changes: can → **could**.
Say it 'kud': the **l** is silent, like in *would*.

steps.title: Then and now
steps.text: Look at Dimas's life. **could / couldn't** for the past, **can** for now.

timeline.title: Dimas: then and now
timeline.caption: Past = could / couldn't. Now = can / can't.

marks.label: When I was five: I could swim

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Bu Ani is talking about her grandmother. Which word fits?

question.prompt: When my grandmother was young, she ___ dance very well.
question.explanation: **When my grandmother was young** is the past, so use **could**, not can. And the verb comes straight after it, with no **to**: **could dance**.

steps.title: Couldn't and questions
steps.text: **Couldn't** is great for telling problems on a trip. Notice the verb after it.
steps.body:
The verb after could/couldn't always stays in the base form: **couldn't open**, not 'couldn't opened'. Could already shows the past, so you don't show it twice.
Questions: **Could** + subject + verb? Short answers: **Yes, I could. / No, I couldn't.** No do/did with could.

examples.en: I couldn't open the door, so I called reception.
examples.id: Saya tidak bisa membuka pintunya, jadi saya menelepon resepsionis.

examples.en: We couldn't find a taxi, so we walked to the hotel.
examples.id: Kami tidak bisa menemukan taksi, jadi kami jalan kaki ke hotel.

examples.en: My grandfather couldn't read, but he could fix any motorbike.
examples.id: Kakek saya tidak bisa membaca, tapi dia bisa memperbaiki motor apa saja.

examples.en: Could you swim when you were five? — Yes, I could.
examples.id: Kamu sudah bisa berenang waktu umur lima tahun? — Ya, bisa.

steps.title: A rainy holiday
steps.text: Sari and her friends were in Bali, but the weather was bad.

question.prompt: It rained all day, so we ___ to the beach.
question.explanation: After **couldn't** the verb stays in the base form: **couldn't go**. *Went* is the past of go, but could already shows the past, so 'couldn't went' is wrong. And there is no did with could.

steps.title: Polite requests: Could you …?
steps.text: Could has another job. **Could you …?** asks someone to help you, like **Can you …?**, but more politely.
steps.body:
Pattern: **Could you** + base verb … **please**? Use it with strangers, hotel staff or your boss.
Isn't could the past? Not here: a request is about **now**. A past-looking word makes the question softer, so it sounds more polite, like adding *kira-kira* in Indonesian. Past ability has a past time (*when you were five*); a request doesn't.
Yes: **Sure. / Of course.** No: **Sorry, I can't** + a reason.

pairs.en: Could you say that again, please?

steps.title: Build a request
steps.text: You're on holiday in Bandung with your family. You want a stranger to take a picture of all of you.

question.prompt: Arrange the words: Bisa tolong fotokan kami?
question.solution: Could you take a photo of us?
question.explanation: A polite request is **Could you** + base verb …? So: **Could you take a photo of us?** *Us* = kami, after *of*.

steps.title: Saying no
steps.text: At the airport, a man with two big suitcases asks you: 'Could you help me with my bags?' But your flight leaves in ten minutes.

options: Sorry, I can't. I'm late for my flight.
Sorry, I couldn't. I'm late for my flight.
Sorry, you can't. I'm late for my flight.
question.explanation: The request is about **now**, so say no with **Sorry, I can't**. 'I couldn't' sounds like the past, and 'you can't' refuses permission, which is not what he asked.

steps.title: Asking permission: Could I …?
steps.text: And with **I**, could asks for permission politely, like *boleh saya …?*
steps.body:
Pattern: **Could I** + base verb …? It's about **now** too: *Could I open the window?* = *Boleh saya buka jendelanya?* Could just makes **Can I …?** more polite.
Yes: **Yes, of course. / Sure, go ahead.** (*go ahead* = silakan) or **Yes, you can.**
No: **Sorry, you can't** + a reason.
Answer with **can**, not could, and with **you**, not I.

steps.title: At the homestay
steps.text: You're staying at a homestay in Bali. You want to cook some noodles in the owner's kitchen. What do you ask the owner?

options: Do I could use the kitchen?
question.explanation: You ask permission for yourself, so use **Could I** …? There is no **do** with could, and **Could you** …? asks the owner to do something.

steps.title: Cheat sheet
steps.text: Here's everything on one page. Take it on your next trip!

artifact.title: Cheat sheet · could
artifact.intro: Could has two jobs: past ability (dulu bisa) and polite requests or permission (now). Always could + base verb.
rows: When I was five, I could swim.
Could you swim when you were five? — Yes, I could.
Could you help me, please? — Sure. / Sorry, I can't.
Could I open the window? — Sure, go ahead.
Sorry, you can't. It's for guests only.
tips: Could + base verb: **could go**, **couldn't open** (not 'couldn't went', not 'could to go').
**Could you / Could I** are about now: could only makes them more polite than can.
Answer with **can**: Sorry, I can't. / Yes, you can (not 'Yes, you could').

examples.en: My grandfather couldn't read, but he could fix any motorbike.
examples.id: Kakek saya tidak bisa membaca, tapi dia bisa memperbaiki motor apa saja.

examples.en: Could you say that again, please?
Could I pay by card? — Yes, of course.
examples.id: Boleh saya bayar pakai kartu? — Ya, tentu.

id.greeting: Hai! Kamu sudah kenal can. Hari ini kamu bertemu pasangannya yang sopan dan bisa untuk masa lalu: could. Ayo mulai!

steps.title: Could: can di masa lalu
steps.text: Can untuk sekarang: **I can swim.** Untuk masa lalu, bahasa Inggris mengganti katanya menjadi **could**.
steps.body:
**could** = *dulu bisa*, **couldn't** (could not) = *dulu tidak bisa*. Seperti can, could adalah kata bantu: sama untuk semua orang, dan kata kerja sesudahnya tetap bentuk dasar (tanpa -s, tanpa -ed, tanpa to): **When I was five, I could swim.**
Jebakannya: dalam bahasa Indonesia *bisa* tidak pernah berubah (*dulu saya bisa …*). Dalam bahasa Inggris katanya berubah: can → **could**.
Dibaca 'kud': huruf **l** tidak dibaca, sama seperti *would*.

steps.title: Dulu dan sekarang
steps.text: Lihat kehidupan Dimas. **could / couldn't** untuk masa lalu, **can** untuk sekarang.

timeline.title: Dimas: dulu dan sekarang
timeline.caption: Masa lalu = could / couldn't. Sekarang = can / can't.

marks.label: When I was five: I could swim

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Bu Ani bercerita tentang neneknya. Kata mana yang cocok?

question.prompt: Lengkapi: When my grandmother was young, she ___ dance very well.
question.explanation: **When my grandmother was young** (waktu nenek saya masih muda) adalah masa lalu, jadi pakai **could**, bukan can. Dan kata kerjanya langsung sesudahnya, tanpa **to**: **could dance**.

steps.title: Couldn't dan pertanyaan
steps.text: **Couldn't** sangat pas untuk menceritakan masalah dalam perjalanan. Perhatikan kata kerja sesudahnya.
steps.body:
Kata kerja sesudah could/couldn't selalu tetap bentuk dasar: **couldn't open**, bukan 'couldn't opened'. Could sudah menunjukkan masa lalu, jadi masa lalunya tidak ditunjukkan dua kali.
Pertanyaan: **Could** + subjek + kata kerja? Jawaban singkat: **Yes, I could. / No, I couldn't.** Tidak ada do/did kalau memakai could.

examples.en: I couldn't open the door, so I called reception.
examples.id: Saya tidak bisa membuka pintunya, jadi saya menelepon resepsionis.

examples.en: We couldn't find a taxi, so we walked to the hotel.
examples.id: Kami tidak bisa menemukan taksi, jadi kami jalan kaki ke hotel.

examples.en: My grandfather couldn't read, but he could fix any motorbike.
examples.id: Kakek saya tidak bisa membaca, tapi dia bisa memperbaiki motor apa saja.

examples.en: Could you swim when you were five? — Yes, I could.
examples.id: Kamu sudah bisa berenang waktu umur lima tahun? — Ya, bisa.

steps.title: Liburan yang hujan
steps.text: Sari dan teman-temannya di Bali, tapi cuacanya buruk.

question.prompt: Lengkapi: It rained all day, so we ___ to the beach.
question.explanation: Sesudah **couldn't**, kata kerjanya tetap bentuk dasar: **couldn't go**. *Went* memang bentuk lampau dari go, tapi could sudah menunjukkan masa lalu, jadi 'couldn't went' salah. Dan tidak ada did kalau memakai could.

steps.title: Meminta tolong dengan sopan: Could you …?
steps.text: Could punya tugas lain. **Could you …?** meminta orang membantumu, seperti **Can you …?**, tapi lebih sopan.
steps.body:
Pola: **Could you** + kata kerja dasar … **please**? Pakai untuk orang yang tidak dikenal, petugas hotel atau atasanmu.
Bukankah could itu masa lalu? Di sini bukan: permintaan tolong itu tentang **sekarang**. Kata yang bentuknya seperti masa lalu membuat pertanyaan lebih lembut, jadi terdengar lebih sopan, mirip menambahkan *kira-kira*. Kemampuan masa lalu punya keterangan waktu lampau (*when you were five*); permintaan tolong tidak.
Ya: **Sure. / Of course.** Tidak: **Sorry, I can't** + alasan.

pairs.en: Could you say that again, please?

steps.title: Susun permintaannya
steps.text: Kamu sedang berlibur di Bandung bersama keluargamu. Kamu ingin minta tolong orang yang tidak dikenal untuk memotret kalian semua.

question.prompt: Susun kata-katanya: Bisa tolong fotokan kami?
question.solution: Could you take a photo of us?
question.explanation: Permintaan tolong yang sopan = **Could you** + kata kerja dasar …? Jadi: **Could you take a photo of us?** *Us* = kami, sesudah *of*.

steps.title: Menolak dengan sopan
steps.text: Di bandara, seorang laki-laki dengan dua koper besar bertanya kepadamu: 'Could you help me with my bags?' Tapi pesawatmu berangkat sepuluh menit lagi.

options: Sorry, I can't. I'm late for my flight.
Sorry, I couldn't. I'm late for my flight.
Sorry, you can't. I'm late for my flight.
question.explanation: Permintaannya tentang **sekarang**, jadi tolak dengan **Sorry, I can't**. 'I couldn't' terdengar seperti masa lalu, dan 'you can't' berarti tidak memberi izin, padahal dia tidak meminta izin.

steps.title: Meminta izin: Could I …?
steps.text: Dan dengan **I**, could meminta izin dengan sopan, seperti *boleh saya …?*
steps.body:
Pola: **Could I** + kata kerja dasar …? Ini juga tentang **sekarang**: *Could I open the window?* = *Boleh saya buka jendelanya?* Could hanya membuat **Can I …?** lebih sopan.
Ya: **Yes, of course. / Sure, go ahead.** (*go ahead* = silakan) atau **Yes, you can.**
Tidak: **Sorry, you can't** + alasan.
Jawab dengan **can**, bukan could, dan dengan **you**, bukan I.

steps.title: Di homestay
steps.text: Kamu menginap di sebuah homestay di Bali. Kamu ingin memasak mi di dapur pemiliknya. Apa yang kamu tanyakan kepada pemiliknya?

options: Do I could use the kitchen?
question.explanation: Kamu meminta izin untuk dirimu sendiri, jadi pakai **Could I** …? Tidak ada **do** kalau memakai could, dan **Could you** …? meminta pemiliknya melakukan sesuatu.

steps.title: Ringkasan
steps.text: Ini semuanya dalam satu halaman. Bawa saat kamu bepergian nanti!
